newsitem.title: USA: Washington National Airport opens new terminal.
newsitem.headline: Washington National Airport opens new terminal.

text.p: Washington National Airport's long-awaited stylish new $450 million terminal officially opened for business on Sunday.
"This airport is a symbol of our strong presence and our visionary future," Rodney Slater, secretary of transportation said at the official unveiling of the new terminal.

The facelift includes five-story windows showcasing the Potomac River and a view of the capital along with $5.5 million in artworks including mosaic circles in the floor. There are also dozens of retail shops and restaurants.
Addressing decades-old complaints about National's short runways and restricted areas that planes can't fly over, Slater told ABC's This Week the airport is "going to be a lot safer."

"One of the other improvements is a $25 million tower," he said. "It's a new tower. It's twice as large as the old tower. It will give all of the air traffic controllers a much better view of the airspace."

Slater also cited surface radar detection equipment giving air traffic controllers an important tool for dealing with less than ideal weather and a state-of-the-art communication system allowing better two-way communication with the pilots.

U.S. Airways flight #1721 from Albany, New York made history as the designated first "official" flight to land at the new terminal, arriving at 8:21 a.m, a few minutes earlier than scheduled, the airline said.
The main terminal, built in 1941, is also scheduled to undergo renovations, but no timetable has been set.
